JUDGMENT

This is a petition filed u/s 166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act and Rule 232 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules claiming for compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest from respondents on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.

2. The petitioner's case in brief:

1

That on 29112020 at about 1200 a.m.. when the petitioner was tavelling towards Huliyurudurga side as a pillion rider in his motor bike bearing Reg.No.KA02EU 3701 from Madappanahalli side, near Kembarapalya on the left side of the SH33,
TumakruMadduru road, at that time, rider ofthe bike bearing Reg.No.KA06HJ 2942 came from JUDGMENT Santhemavathuru side with high speed and rash and negligent manner and dashed agaisnt the motor bike from back side in which petitioenr was travelling.
Due to accident, peittioenr sustained grievous injury.

Immediately the petitioner was shifted to CHC, Kunigal hospital wherein doctors advised him for higher hospital for further more treatment and petitoner was shifted to Spinecare and ortho care hospital, Bengaluru wherein he took tretment as inpatient.

entities.text: Spinecare and ortho care hospital, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner has spent Rs.8 lakhs for treatment.

At the time of accident,
the petitioner was hale and healthy and was doing Agriculture and was earning Rs.5,00,000/ p.a. and Rs.15,000/ p.m. from cattle busines and due to accidental injury he is not able to do his work.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.30 lakhs from the respondents.
3. 1st respondent remained absent.
Second respondent in the written statement denied the case of the petitioner, further contended that there was no rashness or negligence on the part of the rider of the bike.
The petitioenr sustained injuries due to fall from motor cycle bearing No.KA02EU JUDGMENT 3701 in which he was pillion rider.
Further contended that jurisdictionl polcie have creted false records and story about the manner and involvement of motor yccle to get comepsnation and lodged a false complaint.
On the date of accidnet the rider of the motor cycle looks out vehicular ovements of the road and without noticing on comign and caused the accident.
As such accidnet took placedue to neglgience onthe part of the petitioenr and not due to the negigence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle.
Further contended that it has issued a policy of insurance in respect of motor cycle bearing No.KA06HJ2942 which is valid on the date of accident.
The liability of the 2 nd respondent would not arise in the instant case for non compliance of the statutory provisions of Section 134 and Section 158 (6) of the MV Act.
Hence prays to dismiss the claim petition with costs.

4. From the above said pleadings three Issues are framed:
ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to JUDGMENT rash and negligent driving of the rider of the bike bearing Reg.Two wheeler No.KA06HJ2942 on 28112020 at about 12.00 a.m. at near Kembarepalya gate, on SH33 road, Huliyurudurga hobli, Kunigal Taluk,Tumkur?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
Puttaswamy vs Prasanthadas on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21627516/
2 5.
The petitioner examined himself as P.W.1 and in his support P.W.2 is examined.
Exs. P1
to P18 documents are marked.
On the other hand 1 st respondent neither adduced oral evidence or produced any documents.

Respodnent No.2 got examined one witness as RW1 and got marked Ex R1.
6.
Heard arguments and perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. My answers to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative, Issue No.3 : As per final order JUDGMENT for the following: REASONS 8.

ISSUE NO.1 : In order to prove that the accident had occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of bike bearing Reg.Two wheeler No.KA06HJ 2942, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 18 documents as ExP1 to 18 i.e.,FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet, adhaar card, discharge summaries, medical bills, RTC copies, xrays and OPD record.

9. The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint lodged by one Devaraja S/o Puttaswamy the Huliyurdurga town police conducted a thorough and detailed investigation and filed ExP6 charge sheet against the rider of the bike bearing Reg.No.KA06HJ2942 for the offenses punishable under Sec's.279, 338 of IPC, holding that accident in question has been taken place due to the the rash & negligent driving of the rider of offending bike bearing Reg.No.KA06 HJ2942.
There is JUDGMENT nothing on record to believe that the chargesheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
10. On Perusal of the cross examination by the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2/Insurance company goes to show that the factum of accident is not denied by it.

Only suggestions were made to the effect that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and not due to the negligence of the rider of bike bearing Reg.No.KA06HJ2942,
which were out rightly denied.
Moreover the respondent No.2 got examined one Abhijith H.Kulali as RW1 and has produced MLC book as ExR1.
Under such circumstances oral evidence coupled with documentary evidence produced by the petitioner has to be accepted.

11. Further on perusal of the ExP3 spot mahazar it clearly shows that rider of the bike bearing Reg.No.KA06 HJ2942 came from back with high speed from Kunigal to Huliyurdurga side and dashed to hind portion of the motor cycle in which petitioner was pillion rider and due to impact petitioner sustained grievous injuries to his right leg.
Even JUDGMENT there is no explanations forthcoming why rider of bike bearing Reg.No.KA06HJ2942 came to his wrong side that is right side of the road.
Moreover all the police documents including the ExP3 is not all disputed by the respondents.
12. Further Ex.P3 Spot mahazar fortifies the fact the impugned accident occurred at the spot mentioned in the petition.

Ex.P5 IMV report indicates that the occurrence of the said accident was Puttaswamy vs Prasanthadas on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21627516/
3 not due to any of the mechanical defects of the motor vehicles involved in the accident.
Ex . P4
wound certificate and discharge summaries marked at Ex.P8 to 10 disclose that the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
The aforementioned documentary evidence is not controverted by the respondents.
Hence there is no reason to disbelieve the same.
Though the respondents have denied the cause of the accident, they have not let in any cogent evidence to prove their defense or to disprove the evidence led by the petitioner.

13. Apart from this, respondent No.2 has examined RW1 Abhijith H.Kulali and produced ExR1 the MLC record JUDGMENT and argued that as per ExR1 on that day one Puttaswamanna S/o Late.Thyagarajaiah, Huliyurdurga was admitted in the hospital and it was not the petitioner as petitioner's name is Puttaswamy S/o Late.Tapasa Shetty.

In this regard, RW1 was cross examined by the petitioner's counsel wherein RW1 admitted that she has produced ExR1 in respect of the patient Puttaswamy and the person who came along with the injured has given the information and one Prashanth Das has accompanied the Puttaswamy ad the accident had been occurred on 2811 2020.
Further RW1 stated that on that day only one person by name Puttaswamy was admitted in the hospital and no other person by name Puttaswamy was admitted in their hospital.

In this regard,
on perusal of the materials on record, the accident had been occurred on 29112020 at around 12.00 am i.e., midnight of 28112020 and further the Prashanth Das who accompanied the petitioner is non other than the respondent No.1 RC owner of the two wheeler.
Further looking into the injuries mentioned in ExR1 they tally with the injuries mentioned in the wound certificate and the JUDGMENT discharge summary of the petitioner.
As such from the abvoe evidence it is clear that ExR1 MLC register relates to the petitioner only.
14. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.

Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the rider of bike bearing Reg.No.KA06HJ2942.
15.

Even otherwise, it is a settled law that in a claim petition, the claimant need not prove the happening of events beyond reasonable doubt and the rule of preponderance of probability would apply in such cases.

In the decision reported in AIR 2009 SC 2819 (Bimla Devi & others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others), it has been held that in a Road accident, the strict principles of proof as in a Criminal case are not attracted.

entities.text: AIR 2009 SC 2819 (Bimla Devi & others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant portion of the said decision is reproduced as follows:
JUDGMENT "15.
In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular Bus, in a particular manner, may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of Proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".

4 16.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in another decision reported in AIR 1980 SC 1354 (N.K.V.Bros. (P) Ltd.
V/s M.Karumai Ammal & others), observed that "Court/Tribunal should not succumb to nicety,
technicalities & mystic.

entities.text:
AIR 1980 SC 1354 (N.K.V.Bros. (P) Ltd.
V/s M.Karumai Ammal & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Special care must be taken to see that innocent victims do not suffer and drivers & owners do not escape liability merely because of some doubt here or obscurity there.
Except in plain cases, culpability must be inferred from the circumstances where it is reasonable".

17. The point that merits consideration is that the degree of proof required for proving the negligence on the JUDGMENT part of the rider of bike bearing Reg.No.KA06HJ2942 in the present proceedings, is not as vigorous as is laid in proving the guilt of the accused in criminal trial.

The intent of the Motor Vehicles Act is benevolent and the entire purpose of the Legislation is likely to be defeated if in each case the petitioner is asked to prove the involvement and negligence on the part of the driver beyond reasonable doubt.

18. Therefore by applying the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in the decisions cited supra, to the facts of the instant proceedings, this Tribunal is of the opinion that petitioner had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident caused by the rider of bike bearing Reg.No.KA06 HJ2942 on account of his rash & negligent riding.
Hence issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2 :
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident took place due to the actionable negligence of the rider of two wheeler bearing JUDGMENT reg.No.KA06 HJ2942.
Therefore the petitioner is entitled for compensation.
20. AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME :
So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that at the time of accident he was aged 60 years.
The petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.7, it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner as 1951 and the accident took place on 28112020.
So, as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged 69 years.
The petitioner has deposed that prior to the accident he was doing agriculture thereby earning an income of Rs.5,00,000/p.a. and Rs.15,000/ p.m. by doing cattle business.
The petitioner has produced ExP13RTC which indicates that land Sy.No.20/1 measuring 0.25 acres stands in the name of Puttaswamy.
But agriculture is a permanent source of income.
As such there is no loss of income to the petitioner from the agriculture.
But the petitioner has not produced any document to prove his income.
Therefore, the income of the petitioner has to be taken into consideration as notional income.

In the absence JUDGMENT of proof taking into consideration the date of accident,
age of the petitioner and nature of her work, if his income is assessed at Rs.14,500/ p.m, it would meet the ends of justice.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:

As per the medical records the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : i.e., compound fracture both bone, right leg and lacerated wound over the dorsum of right leg with loss of blerd celaceneal to the skins.
The doctor has mentioned in the wound certificate that the said injuries are grievous in nature.
It is needless to say that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

Ex.P 8 to 10 discloses that for the aforesaid injuries, the petitioner has taken treatment as inpatient at Spine care and Ortho care hospital, Bengaluru for three times for total period of 41 days and underwent three surgeries.

sentences.text:

5 22.
It is the specific case of the petitioner that owing to the accidental injuries he has become disabled and has lost his earning capacity.

Therefore he got examined JUDGMENT Dr.S.A.Somashekaraas PW.2 who stated that on clinical examination conducted by him, he found that petitioner has sustained the total disability of right lower limb at 52% and for wholebody at 26%.
However from the careful examination of the medical records, it is seen that PW.2 has assessed the disability on the higher side.

Be that as it may, the law is well settled that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.

With regard to the disability in RTA cases, the same has to be assessed on the principles laid down in 2011(1) Supreme Court cases 343 in between Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another wherein it has been held as follows ; A.
Motor Vehicles Act 1988,  Ss.166, 163A and Sch.II - Permanent disability - Compensation - Award of - Assessment of loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability - Detailed principles for, laid down - Functional disability as operative criterion distinguished from physical disability - Disability certificate - Mode of JUDGMENT assessment based upon - Types of disability, distinguished - held, in disability certificate extent of disability of a limb (or part of the body) cannot be assumed to be extent of disability of whole body - Tribunal should not mechanically apply percentage of permanent physical disability as percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity, but must assess functional disability - Directions given to Tribunals in respect of procedure/steps to be followed in such cases - Tort Law - Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, Ss.3, 4 and Schs.I and IV.
B. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Ss.166, 163A and Sch.II - Permanent disability - Compensation - Injured claimant, cheese vendor, sustaining fracture of both bones of left leg and fracture of left radius - Tribunal assuming 45% disability as shown in disability certificate as economic disability -

entities.text: Rajkumar vs Ajay Kumar and Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In appeal, high Court rejected increase in compensation on ground that disability certificate as not reliable - sustainability - held, High Court ought not to have rejected disability certificate -
Tribunal overlooked fact that disability certificate referred to 45% disability to left lower limb and not to functional disability of the body
Permanent functional disability of body assessed as 25%, loss of future earning capacity as 25%
In cases of injured claimant with a disability, no need to deduct onethird out of income towards personal and living expenses.
JUDGMENT C. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Ss.166, 163A and Sch.II - Permanent disability - Validity of disability certificate.

D. Motor Vehicles Act 1988 - Ss.166, 163A and Sch.II - Permanent disability - Held, in cases of injured claimant with a disability, no need to deduct one third out of income towards personal and living expenses.

23. Considering the nature of injuries, line of treatment and on appreciation of the clinical findings noted by the doctor, the possibility of the fact that the petitioner may be having economical or functional disability to the extent of 15%, cannot be ruled out.

Therefore, I consider the functional Puttaswamy vs Prasanthadas on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21627516/
6 disability of petitioner at 15%.
As per Sarla Verma's case, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the age group of above 65 age is '5'.
This Tribunal has already assessed the notional income of the petitioner at Rs.14,500/ p.m.
Hence a sum of Rs.1,30,500/ (Rs.14,500 X 12 X 5 X 15/100) which is rounded off to Rs.1,30,500/ is awarded under this head.
JUDGMENT 23. PAIN & SUFFERINGS :

The petitioner has stated that he has sustained severe pain and sufferings due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident and he has taken the treatment as inpatient for 41 days and undergone three operations.

Inspite of the best available treatment,
he has not come to normal position and due to the fracture injuries of right leg,
petitioner is completely, permanently disabled and suffering from deformity and injuries are not properly cured and he has to undergo one more surgery.
Hence petitioner is suffering from with whole physical and mental pain and agony and injuries sustained by him nothing but death blow on part of him.
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner being the old age of 69 years and certainly undergone severe pain and mental agony.
Looking into the nature of the wounds and age of the petiitoner, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.1,50,000/ under this head.
24. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAIDUP PERIOD:

By considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner and JUDGMENT treatment taken by him and duration of his stay in the hospital for 41 days as inpatient, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for at least 6 months.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner it is quite natural that he could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 7 months.
Thus by taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this Tribunal awards Rs.1,01,500/ (14,500 X 7) under the head loss of income during the laid up period.
25. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:

Admittedly, peititoenr has taken the treatment as inpatient for 41 days and undergone three surgeries and certainly, it cannot be disputed that petitioner is dependent on the others and during the course of his treatment the petitioner might have spent more amount towards attendant charges, conveyance, extra nutritious food etc.
Hence a sum of Rs.85,000/ under this head.
JUDGMENT 26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Thereby the petitioner would obviously face disappointment & frustration and also suffer discomfort in enjoying the normal pleasures & joys of human life.
Hence a sum of Rs.50,000/ is awarded under this head.

7 27.
MEDICAL EXPENSES.

As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner got marked the document as per Ex.P.12 i.e.
medical bills for Rs.1,98,613/ and prescriptions.
28.
The respondents have not disputed the said medical bills, except denial suggestion.

Upon considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, the resultant disability suffered by him due to such injuries, I proceed to award Rs.1,98,613/ under the head of medical expenses.
29. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further JUDGMENT treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

30. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Attendant charges, extra : 85,00000 nutritious food & conveyance charges 2 Pain & sufferings : 1,50,00000 3 Loss of income during laid : 1,01,50000 up period 4 Loss of future income due : 1,30,50000 to disability 5 Loss of future amenities & :
50,00000 happiness 6
Medical expenses : 1,98,61300 Total Rs.7,15,61300 31.
INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
32. There is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the JUDGMENT offending Bike bearing Reg No.KA06HJ2942 and respondent No.2 being the insurer thereof are jointly &
severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a.,
from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
33. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
O R D E R
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,15,613=00 with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondent No.2 is hereby directed to deposit total compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

8 JUDGMENT

After deposit of the compensation amount to the petitioner, 40% shall be deposited in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to him through Epayment on proper identification and verification.
However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on his deposit amount from time to time.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
